To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the haem-bound FeIII-NO complex is similar in bacterial and mammalan NOSs, and that the interactions between the substrate and haem-bound NO are different in the ferric and ferrousoxy species.

the Fe-N-O frequencies are similar in mammalian and bacterial NOSs, but that the interactions between the substrates (L-arginine or NOHA) and haem-bound NO are different in the FeIII- and FeII- NO complexes of NOSs.

the Fe-N-O frequencies in the FeIII- and FeII- NO complexes of bacterial NOSs are similar to those of mammalian NOS and that the interactions between NO and L-Arginine and NOHA are different in the FeII and FeIII-NO states.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the haem-bound intermediates of NOSs and the interactions of the intermediates with the substrates.
understanding the interactions between haems, substrates and NO in bacterial and mammal NO synthases.
the characterization of the haem-bound ligands in the bacterial NOS complexes and with the elucidation of their interactions with the haem-bound substrates and products.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Fe-N-O stretching and bending modes of the haem-bound N(omega)-hydroxylated arginine are very similar in the FeIII- and the FeII-N(omega)-hydroxo-arginate complexes, and that the interactions between the substrates, NO and the haem-NO, are different in the two oxidation states of the haem.
the haem-NO complex of NOS has an important role in the catalytic mechanism of NOS.

the FeII- NO and FeIII-NO species in the bacterial NOS have a haem-NO environment very similar to that of the mammalian enzyme, and that the substrate binding to the haem-bound-NO species is similar in the bacterial and mammalian enzymes, except for the lack of a significant effect of the tetrahydrobiopterin binding on the FeIII- NO species in the bacterial enzyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the FeIII- and FeII- bound NO complexes with the substrates of NOSs display different spectral properties, which reflect the different interactions between haem-NO and the substrates in these enzyme complexes.
the interactions between substrates and haem-bound NO in NOSs are similar in bacterial and mammalan enzymes, and that NOHA is more tightly bound to the FeII- NO complex

the haem-bound ligands of NOSs, L-arginine/NOHA, NO and the oxygenated complex, have similar Fe-ligand structures, which are not significantly affected by the different protein environment in mammalian and bacterial NOSs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the haem-bound substrate NO and the haem-FeII-NO complex have a similar environment, which is consistent with a mechanism involving the direct binding of NO to the FeII-hydroxy-arginine complex.
the haem-bound substrate NO is a good reporter of the haem environment and can be used to probe the conformational changes of the haem pocket of NOSs.
